content.title: About
content.content: Bulgur is a pre-cooked, dried, and coarsely ground wheat of the hard varieties (triticale). It is widely used in Middle Eastern, Mediterranean and Caucasian cuisines. Bulgur has a light nutty flavor, pleasant texture and cooks quickly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bulgur dates back to ancient Egypt where it was used in ceremonial dishes.
Unlike couscous, bulgur is not steamed before drying, preserving more nutrients.
It comes in several grinds: fine (for couscous), medium (for tabbouleh) and coarse (for soups).
Bulgur is often used as a rice or couscous substitute in diet meals.
When kept dry, it can be stored for up to 2 years.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fiber support digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide a slow, steady release of energy, helpful for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3 and B6 vitamins aid carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Bulgur supplies iron, magnesium, phosphorus and zinc, important for blood, bones and immunity.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: It contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Bulgur is made from wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: It contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

items.title: Food allergies
items.content: Rarely, wheat‑sensitive individuals may experience an allergic reaction.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bulgur can be used as a side dish, added to salads (tabbouleh), soups, meat fillings and patties. Typically the grains are rinsed, soaked for 15‑30 minutes, then boiled 10‑15 minutes until tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bulgur in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from moisture and light. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator.
